newsitem.title: POLAND: VILNIUS WANTS PRESIDENTIAL MEETING WITH LUKASHENKO.
newsitem.headline: VILNIUS WANTS PRESIDENTIAL MEETING WITH LUKASHENKO.

text.p: Vilnius has proposed that the Lithuanian, Polish and Ukrainian presidents jointly meet their Belarus counterpart Alexander Lukashenko next week, Poland's Aleksander Kwasniewski said on Thursday.

But even as the Polish president revealed Lithuania's idea for a meeting on the sidelines of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation's (OSCE) Lisbon summit, he suggested such a move could do little to help ease the tension in Belarus.

"Lithuania just... made a proposal, which we will examine but over which I am sceptical, that the three presidents might meet with the president of Belarus who will be there," Kwasniewski told a news briefing ahead of the OSCE meeting.
"I would not really see a good conclusion, or even much sense to such a discussion," he added.
Kwasniewski, Lithuania's Algirdas Brazauskas and Ukraine's Leonid Kuchma issued a statement earlier this month calling for a constitutional resolution of the crisis in Belarus.
Since then, Lukashenko has won greater powers in a controversial referendum, then overseen the creation of a new legislature to rival the parliament where some members fiercely opposed him.
Kwasniewski said the joint statement by the countries neighbouring Belarus had evoked international praise and the three leaders would further discuss the issue in Lisbon.
He said the democracy, sovereignty and development of Belarus had a bearing on the whole region, the countries of which therefore carried special responsibilities.
"Democracy in Belarus is such an important matter that it cannot just be left up to President Lukashenko," he said.
Poland is deeply concerned over instability in Belarus, where it has considerable interests, with which it shares a long land border, and which has a Polish minority.
Kwasniewski said it was important not to isolate Belarus.

"But support for Belarus must be associated with respect for human rights there, respecting the basis of democracy," said Kwasniewski, adding that Russia, the United States and other countries had a crucial role to play.
Kwasniewski was not entirely gloomy over Belarus, suggesting that there were politicians associated with Lukashenko who might be open to some compromise.
"We have to expect that political forces will be found, including ones near President Lukashenko, who will help to find a way out of this deadlock," Kwasniewski said.
The Polish president applauded the removal from Belarus of the last missile from the former Soviet Union's once-mighty nuclear arsenal stationed there.
"I regard this as a clear signal that Belarus does not want to lose contact with international society," he said.
But in answer to a question, Kwasniewski said Poland would grant asylum to political refugees from Belarus if necessary.

Kwasniewski said that in Lisbon he would outline longer term proposals, to be promoted by Poland when it assumes the OSCE presidency in 1998, to define and strengthen the body's role in quickly identifying and dealing with crisis hot spots.
